clue.text: Make out, staying in, you finally try fast food

indicators.note: staying is read as a container signal: the following pieces stay within the rearranged word
out signals that the letters of the word make are put out of their order
finally picks the last letter of the word you

parts.note: to try something is to test it

explanation.surface: A slangy instruction: snog for a bit, stay home, and then grab a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make out' reads as snogging, but 'out' is the anagram signal on 'Make' alone, and 'staying' is the container signal holding the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute steak is a thin cut cooked in about a minute, so it counts as quick fare.

clue.text: Party to start from our pub walls

indicators.note: walls says the pub surrounds the letter

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: start from takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A party begins at the local, then spreads from its walls.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in on something is to be party to it, sharing in a secret or plan.

clue.text: Toff maybe owned up to shilly-shally

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, so a toff is a U man

indicators.note: up reads the word upwards, backwards in a down clue

parts.note: owned means had

explanation.surface: A posh person finally confesses he was a ditherer.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were labels for upper-class and non-upper-class usage, so a toff is a U-man.
explanation.definitionFit: To um and ah is to hesitate and dither, the same as to shilly-shally.

clue.text: Different term for the University of London

indicators.note: term means end, so the last letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: LSE is the London School of Economics, part of the University of London

explanation.surface: A query about another name for the University of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term' looks like an academic term or a word; here it means the end of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Else means other or different, as in somewhere else.

clue.text: Unerringly squashes bug that's buzzing around tower

indicators.note: squashes says the outer phrase presses the other letters inside it

parts.note: to a T means exactly, without error

indicators.note: buzzing around suggests the letters of bug fly about in a new order

explanation.surface: A swatter flattens a buzzing insect circling a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' is read as one who tows, not a tall building.
explanation.definitionFit: A tugboat tows ships, so it is literally a tower.

clue.text: Where one goes after a curry dish

indicators.note: after puts the toilet after the letter A

parts.note: the loo is where one goes, a coy phrase for the toilet

explanation.surface: Where you end up heading after a hot curry.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jokes about a curry's aftermath.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloo is potato in Indian cookery, as in aloo gobi, a curry dish.

clue.text: Modify widget with borer and adjustable spanner

indicators.note: Modify tells us to change the order of the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A mechanic tweaks a gadget using a drill and a wrench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjustable spanner' looks like a tool; it is a bridge that spans the Thames and opens.
explanation.definitionFit: Tower Bridge spans the Thames and its bascules lift, so it is a spanner that adjusts.

clue.text: OK, now pass through tight doors with furniture item

indicators.note: with puts the furniture item beside the rest, here at the front

parts.note: a sofa is an item of furniture

indicators.note: through says one piece passes inside the other
tight, as in drunk, signals that the letters of doors are scrambled

parts.note: to pass is to go

explanation.surface: Someone manoeuvring a sofa through a narrow doorway reports progress so far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' means drunk here, the anagram signal; 'through' is the container and 'with' sets the furniture first. The definition is the two words 'OK, now'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said when things have gone well up to the present moment, an all-right-for-now verdict.

clue.text: 'Resemblances' contains B just once and 'balance beam world-beater' three times

indicators.note: contains says the other letters go inside

parts.note: similes are figures of speech drawing resemblances
just once is one time, giving one

explanation.surface: A wordplay puzzle about how often letters appear in a phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rides on the quotes: the gymnast won the world title on the balance beam three times.
explanation.definitionFit: The American gymnast won the world championship on the balance beam three times.

clue.text: Seduce married man where artist prepares sitter?

parts.note: to draw someone in is to lure or seduce them
a groom is a man just married

explanation.surface: An artist lures in a married man to pose for a portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is whimsical: a room for drawing, and a room for sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing room is a formal sitting room, and read literally a room for drawing a model.

clue.text: Low-down on MoMA perhaps protected by a spoiler

indicators.note: protected by says the per wraps round the rest

parts.note: per means a, as in 'twice per day'

indicators.note: on means about, so the info about the arty place is written with its subject first

parts.note: MoMA, New York's Museum of Modern Art, is an arty place
poop is slang for the low-down, inside information

explanation.surface: Gossip about a museum hidden inside a film spoiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arty poop' is whimsical inside information on an art museum.
explanation.definitionFit: A party pooper spoils other people's fun, a killjoy.

clue.text: Perform turns because of God

indicators.note: turns tells us the word for perform is read backwards

parts.note: to perform a task is to do it
in can mean because of, as in 'in that' or 'in view of'

explanation.surface: An actor performs a turn on stage because a deity demands it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' makes DO into OD.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology.

clue.text: In our array, there's nothing even or odd for Napier

indicators.note: nothing in the even positions is kept, so only the odd-placed letters of the phrase remain

explanation.surface: A mathematician like John Napier sorts an array into odd and even entries.
explanation.walkthrough: John Napier, inventor of logarithms, was a Scot, so 'for Napier' asks for a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Orra is a Scots word meaning odd or spare, as in an orra man doing odd jobs.

clue.text: Boy who's collared ain't one for caning

indicators.note: caning means beating, so the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A schoolboy grabbed by the collar admits he deserves a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eton collar is a broad white collar worn by Eton College boys, so the collar is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil of Eton College traditionally wore the stiff Eton collar, so he is a boy known for a collar.

clue.text: Object of gazing a little upon a velarium

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone stares up at the awning over an ancient amphitheatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Navel-gazing is self-absorbed contemplation, so the belly button is what is gazed at.

clue.text: Wally and Alfred going for a cycle

indicators.note: going for a cycle says some letters travel round from the front to the back

parts.note: and Alfred is with Alf, Alf being the short form of Alfred

explanation.surface: Two friends, Wally and Alfred, head out for a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally is British slang for a fool; moving WIT from the front of WITH ALF to the end gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a wally is a silly or foolish person, which is what a halfwit is too.

clue.text: Hardy Amies initially struck about clashing part of kit

indicators.note: about says the word for struck goes round

parts.note: struck means hit

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of the designer's name

explanation.surface: A fashion designer strikes out against a clashing outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy Amies was a royal dressmaker; 'kit' is a drum kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A hi-hat is the pair of cymbals clashed together by a pedal in a drum kit.

clue.text: Hotel with not much custom

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
not much is a bit

explanation.surface: A hotel that does little trade with very few customers.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a settled practice, the same as a custom or usual way of doing things.

clue.text: Plot raising a section of 7 Down

indicators.note: raising suggests lifting, as the bascules of the bridge go up, so the picked letters run the other way

parts.note: a run of letters taken from inside the answer to 7 Down, the London landmark

explanation.surface: A scheme to lift one part of a famous bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside TO(WERB)RIDGE sits WERB; 'raising' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To brew trouble is to plot it, as when a storm or a scheme is brewing.

clue.text: Review criticises game of little skill

indicators.note: Review is read as re-view, looking back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a game as needing little skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Review' looks like a noun to do with critics; it turns PANS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap is a children's card game won by quick reactions rather than thought or skill.

clue.text: Remove nitrous oxide, say, from impressionist

definitions.meaning: to take gas out of something; nitrous oxide is one example of a gas
Edgar ... was a French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: Someone tries to strip laughing gas from a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Degassing removes gas from a substance; Degas painted ballet dancers in the Impressionist circle.

clue.text: Sorcerer opens pop with leak in can?

indicators.note: opens says one piece breaks into the other

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for father, dad
a mage is a wizard or sorcerer

explanation.surface: A wizard opens a fizzy drink and finds the can is leaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' looks like fizzy drink beside 'can', but it means father.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin that leaks is an example of something harmed, hence the question mark.

clue.text: A little secretive about choice of openers for Headingley Test

indicators.note: about says the secretive word wraps round the rest

parts.note: sly means secretive or cunning

parts.words: choice of openers for Headingley Test
parts.note: the openers, or first letters, of Headingley and Test offered as alternatives: one or the other

explanation.surface: A slightly cagey selection of opening batsmen for a cricket Test at Headingley.
explanation.walkthrough: Headingley is a Leeds cricket ground. 'choice of openers' reads as H OR T, either initial, which 'about' places inside SLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortly means in a little while, soon.

clue.text: First enjoying success, it all evens out

parts.note: someone in it is in the money, doing well

indicators.note: evens out means the even-placed letters are taken out, leaving the odd ones

explanation.surface: An early win that everything later balances out.
explanation.walkthrough: From I-T-A-L-L, 'evens out' drops T and L, leaving IAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means first, as in the initial stage of something.

clue.text: Nasty slur withdrawn from soul brother playing instrument

indicators.note: Nasty signals the letters of slur are mixed up before being removed
withdrawn from says the slur's letters come out of the soul brother's
playing signals the letters of soul brother are set loose in a new order

explanation.surface: An offensive remark is taken back from a musician friend's performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of SLUR ('Nasty') out of the letters of SOUL BROTHER ('playing'), and the leftover letters rearrange into the answer; 'withdrawn from' signals the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorbo is a large bass lute with an extended neck, used in Baroque music.

clue.text: Welshwoman second of agents subverted

indicators.note: second of points at the second letter of the agents
subverted is read as turned upside down, which flips one letter into another

parts.note: G-men are FBI agents

explanation.surface: A Welsh woman agent turns double against her colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second of' takes M in G-MEN and 'subverted' turns it upside down into W.
explanation.definitionFit: Gwen is a Welsh female name, short for Gwendolen or Gwenllian.

clue.text: From underside, cored shallot? That's forbidden …

indicators.note: From underside reads the word from its bottom upwards, backwards in a down clue
cored means the central letter is taken away

parts.note: a shallot is a kind of onion

explanation.surface: A cook is told off for coring a shallot from beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cored' removes the middle I of ONION, and 'From underside' turns ONON round.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-no is something not allowed, a thing that must not be done.

clue.text: … unlimited port?

parts.note: unlimited is read as nothing banned: a zero followed by a word for a prohibition, naming a Scottish west-coast harbour

explanation.surface: Following 24 Down, a harbour where nothing is forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 24 Down's forbidding: the name split as O BAN reads as zero ban.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a ferry port on the west coast of Scotland, also known for its whisky.

clue.text: I think this work's very heavy

definitions.meaning: ... can mean in my view, as in 'it seems ...'

explanation.surface: Someone lifting a book gives an opinion on its weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer as TO ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large weighty volume, and 'to me' is a phrase introducing an opinion.

clue.text: Removing wrapper, put off frying this?

definitions.text: Removing wrapper, put off frying this?

indicators.note: frying, like cooking, signals the letters are jumbled
removing the wrapper strips the outer letters off the phrase

explanation.surface: A cook unwraps a block of bean curd but cannot face frying it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removing wrapper' leaves UTOF from PUT OFF, and 'frying' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is bean curd sold in a wrapper and often fried, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Counter saw beside horse sizable negative for Mary

indicators.note: Counter means running in the opposite direction, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: a saw is a saying, a motto
by means beside, as in 'stand by me'
gee-gee, written GG, is a child's word for a horse
OS is the abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A wise saying beside a big horse sounds like a strange pronouncement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' reverses the lot. Mary Berry was a judge on The Great British Bake Off, where pastry with an undercooked, damp base is condemned.
explanation.definitionFit: A soggy bottom is the classic baking fault Mary Berry criticised on television.

clue.text: Sweetener for tart in bygone days presented in grand rug

indicators.note: presented in signals one piece set inside another

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
syrup is rhyming slang for a wig, from syrup of figs, and rug is slang for a wig
olden means of bygone days

explanation.surface: Treacle tart sweetened in the old days with something served on a fine rug.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhyming slang: syrup of figs = wig, and rug is also slang for a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden syrup is the pale sugar syrup that fills a treacle tart.
